paper.title: CHAM: A Family of Lightweight Block Ciphers for Resource-Constrained Devices

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm description; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: CHAM-64/128, CHAM-128/128 and CHAM-128/256 encrypt the three Appendix A test vectors to the published ciphertexts (3 of 3)
27 further vectors (9 per variant) that the Crypto++ file labels "CHAM reference implementation" match (27 of 27, 30 of 30 in all)
decrypting each of the 30 ciphertexts returns the plaintext (30 of 30 round trips)

expected_values_source.what: the Crypto++ test-vector file cham.txt: entries labelled "CHAM paper, Appendix A, test vector 1/2/3" (printed word order) and 27 labelled "CHAM reference implementation"
expected_values_source.note: the paper PDF itself was not fetched; the 27 reference-implementation vectors are as labelled by Crypto++ and were not checked against the authors' repository. Data copied as numbers; no code was copied

negative_control: built with CHAM_ROT_A=7 (rotation 7 instead of 8 in the round function), 0 of 3 paper vectors and 0 of 30 vectors match, program exits 1
not_checked: security claims, hardware or software performance figures
other parameter sets (the paper defines only these three)
whether the 27 reference-implementation vectors are the authors' own outputs (taken as labelled)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces the three published CHAM test vectors and 27 more labelled reference vectors and inverts all 30. It does not show the cipher is secure.
